options.title: Why are English cities poorer in the east?
options.first_line: Why is the east side of so many old English cities the poorer side?
options.first_frame: An old map of an English city cut down the middle: the west half in green with big villas, the east half grey with crowded terraces, a big question mark planted on the east.

options.title: Rich west, poor east: why do English cities split?
options.first_line: In England's old industrial cities, the rich side is usually the west and the poor side the east. Why the east?
options.first_frame: A map of England with its old industrial cities pinned, each one splitting into a green west half and a grey east half one after another.

options.title: Why is the East End always the poor end?
options.first_line: Why is the East End of an English city so often the poor end? Look which way the wind blows.
options.first_frame: A city map with a weathervane standing on the town hall, spinning to point east, and the label EAST END writing itself across the grey half.

why: A asks a clear question about a place you can picture, shows it on one split city map without sound, and holds back the answer, while C gives the twist away with the wind and B spends its title stating the pattern.
